title: Time Frames with Adverbs
lede: Use time adverbs and phrases to establish clear past, present, habitual and future meaning in functional communication.
nav: Common Adverbs of Time, Place and Manner

items.prompt: Choose the sentence with a clear past time frame.
items.feedback: Past verb + أمسِ creates a clear past frame.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence with a clear future time frame.
items.feedback: سـ + present form plus غدًا gives explicit future meaning.

items.prompt: Which expression means “at the moment / currently”?
items.feedback: The phrase locates the action in the present period.

items.prompt: Which sentence contains a tense-time mismatch?
items.feedback: Future سـ conflicts with أمسِ unless a very unusual reported context is supplied.

items.prompt: What does a time adverb do?
options: It locates the action in time.
items.feedback: The verb carries tense/person; the adverb gives temporal context.

items.prompt: Which is the clearest IGCSE answer for “I will travel tomorrow”?
items.feedback: A bare present can indicate an arranged future in context, but سـ makes the future explicit and unambiguous.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الطَّبِيبِ.
items.feedback: أمسِ provides past context.

items.prompt: Choose “last week”.
items.feedback: في الأسبوع الماضي is a reliable set phrase.

items.prompt: Choose “I used to / usually studied in the evening” at a simple practical level.
items.feedback: كان + present form can express a past habitual action; this is Develop content.

items.prompt: Which phrase means “the day before yesterday”?
items.feedback: أوّل أمسِ means the day before yesterday.

items.prompt: Repair: زُرْتُهُ غَدًا.
options: Both can repair it, depending on intended time.
items.feedback: Either change the time word to past or change the verb to future.

items.prompt: Choose “I am writing now.”
items.feedback: Present form + الآنَ gives current action.

items.prompt: Choose a habitual present sentence.
items.feedback: كل يوم indicates repeated present routine.

items.prompt: Which word often signals frequency rather than one point in time?
items.feedback: أحيانًا describes how often.

items.prompt: Choose “currently, I live in London.”
options: فِي الْوَقْتِ الْحَالِيِّ أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ.
items.feedback: The current-time phrase matches the present verb.

items.prompt: Which answer is most developed for a speaking question about routine?
items.feedback: The time phrase makes the answer clearer and more informative.

items.prompt: Choose “I will start soon.”
items.feedback: سـ + present form plus قريبًا creates a clear future.

items.prompt: Choose a formal/emphatic future marker.
items.feedback: سوف + present form expresses future.

items.prompt: Choose “I will not be late tomorrow.”
items.feedback: لن + subjunctive negates future; أتأخرَ ends with fatḥa in the supported model.

items.prompt: Which phrase means “next week”?
items.feedback: الأسبوع القادم / المقبل means next week.

items.prompt: Which statement is most accurate?
options: A future time word always makes any past verb future.
The verb and time expression should work together.
سوف is used only with past verbs.
items.feedback: Time frame is built by the combination of verb form, marker and context.

items.prompt: Past: choose the best sentence.
items.feedback: Past verb agrees with أمسِ.

items.prompt: Present now: choose the best sentence.
items.feedback: Present form + الآنَ.

items.prompt: Habit: choose the best sentence.
items.feedback: The phrase signals repeated routine.

items.prompt: Future: choose the best sentence.
items.feedback: Future marker and future adverb match.

items.prompt: Future negative: choose the best sentence.
items.feedback: لن + present/subjunctive form.

items.prompt: Which expression means “until now”?
items.feedback: حتى الآن extends from earlier time to the present.

items.prompt: Choose the arranged-future statement that is possible but less explicit.
items.feedback: Bare present + future time can express an arrangement; سأسافر is clearer for learners.

items.prompt: Repair: سَأَكْتُبُ الرِّسَالَةَ أَمْسِ.
options: Either A or B, depending on intended meaning.
items.feedback: Repair either the verb or the time expression.

items.prompt: Which trio clearly moves through three time frames?
items.feedback: Past, present and future sequence.

items.prompt: Best speaking strategy for a developed answer?
options: Use only one tense even when the question changes.
Add an accurate time marker and match the verb form.
Memorise a time word without a verb.
items.feedback: Accurate time framing makes communication clear.

blocks: ## Why time frames matter

Cambridge speaking and writing require learners to move beyond one-word answers. A precise time expression helps the listener understand whether an event happened, is happening, happens regularly or will happen.
### Core
Match common past, present and future expressions to suitable verbs.
### Develop
Move confidently between three time frames in one answer.
### Stretch
Use past habit, arranged future and future negation with accurate forms.
[callout] The key principle: the time expression does not replace the tense. The verb form, future marker and context must work together.
## Diagnostic timeline
## Past time frame الزَّمَنُ الْمَاضِي
Past time expressions confirm that an event is completed or locate it in an earlier period.

TABLE: Expression | Meaning | Model // أَمْسِ | yesterday | لَعِبْتُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ أَمْسِ. // أَوَّلَ أَمْسِ | the day before yesterday | وَصَلَتِ الرِّسَالَةُ أَوَّلَ أَمْسِ. // فِي الأُسْبُوعِ الْمَاضِي | last week | زُرْنَا الْمَتْحَفَ فِي الأُسْبُوعِ الْمَاضِي. // مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ | for/since a year ago, depending on structure | بَدَأْتُ دِرَاسَةَ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ.
[callout] Develop: كُنْتُ أَدْرُسُ فِي الْمَسَاءِ can describe a past habit: “I used to study in the evening.”
## Present and habitual time الْحَاضِرُ وَالْعَادَةُ
The Arabic present form can describe what is happening now or what happens regularly. The adverbial context makes the intended meaning clear.
### Happening now
أَكْتُبُ الآنَ. فِي الْوَقْتِ الْحَالِيِّ أَعْمَلُ مِنَ الْمَنْزِلِ.
### Regular or repeated
أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. أَتَدَرَّبُ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الأُسْبُوعِ. أَقْرَأُ غَالِبًا قَبْلَ النَّوْمِ.
[callout] Notice: the same present verb form can mean “I study” or “I am studying.” Words such as الآنَ and كُلَّ يَوْمٍ clarify the frame.
## Future time frame زَمَنُ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ
For clear learner communication, combine a future marker with the present verb form and an appropriate future expression.

TABLE: Pattern | Use | Example // سَـ + الْمُضَارِعُ | common, close or neutral future | سَأُسَافِرُ غَدًا. // سَوْفَ + الْمُضَارِعُ | more separate/formal or emphatic future marker | سَوْفَ نَبْدَأُ قَرِيبًا. // لَنْ + الْمُضَارِعُ الْمَنْصُوبُ | future negative | لَنْ أَتَأَخَّرَ غَدًا. // الْمُضَارِعُ + وَقْتٌ مُسْتَقْبَلِيٌّ | possible for an arrangement in context | أُسَافِرُ غَدًا.
[callout/warning] IGCSE clarity: أُسَافِرُ غَدًا can be natural for an arranged plan, but سَأُسَافِرُ غَدًا is clearer and safer when demonstrating future control.
## Three-time-frame communication
### 📖 Reading timeline
أَمْسِ دَرَسْتُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ. الْيَوْمَ أُرَاجِعُ فِي الْبَيْتِ، وَغَدًا سَأَكْتُبُ الْمَشْرُوعَ.
Build a three-column timeline and copy each verb with its time expression.
### 🎧 Listening switch
A partner reads six sentences. Hold up PAST, PRESENT or FUTURE, then quote the word that gave you the clue.
### 🗣️ Topic conversation
Answer: What did you do last weekend? What do you usually do now? What will you do next weekend? Give two developed sentences for each.
### 🛠️ Tense-time repair
Write four mismatched sentences deliberately. Exchange, repair the verb or time phrase, and explain the intended frame.
### ✍️ Past–present–future paragraph
Write 100–120 words about your learning, leisure or travel. Include a completed past event, a present routine/current situation and at least two future plans.
[callout] Model: أَمْسِ أَكْمَلْتُ وَاجِبِي. الْيَوْمَ أُرَاجِعُ دُرُوسِي، وَغَدًا سَأَسْتَعِدُّ لِلِاخْتِبَارِ. لَنْ أَتَأَخَّرَ عَنْ مَوْعِدِي.
[callout] Success checklist: Use at least three past, three present/habitual and three future time expressions; use سـ or سوف clearly; include one future negative with لن as Stretch.
Save and mark complete Clear
Plan a timeline, place map or sentence flowchart, then label it in Arabic with the target adverbs.
Complete the same task on paper. Circle each adverb or adverbial phrase and draw an arrow to the verb or sentence it modifies.
## Final mastery check
### Today you can
- match verbs and time expressions accurately;
- distinguish current action from repeated habit;
- express clear future plans with سـ, سوف and لن;
- develop speaking and writing across three time frames.
